parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the main teachings of Qurʾan 25.68–70.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain how the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) encourage Muslims to repent to
God.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
To what extent should Muslims consider God’s forgiveness more than God’s punishment?
Discuss with reference to different points of view. 
EITHER

text: Read the following text passages, then answer the questions which follow.
Those who invoke not, with Allah, any other god, nor slay such life as Allah has made sacred
except for just cause, nor commit fornication; – and any that does this (not only) meets
punishment. (But) the Penalty on the Day of Judgment will be doubled to him, and he will dwell
therein in ignominy,– Unless he repents, believes, and works righteous deeds, for Allah will
change the evil of such persons into good, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

parts.text: Explain the role of prophets as a connection between God and humans.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘It is easier to understand guidance from prophets than from books.’ Evaluate this statement.

OR

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Examine different rituals of daily prayer in Islam.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Prayer (salah) is the best way to connect to God.’ Do you agree? Discuss with reference to
different points of view.
